facts.statement: The entry treats the first eight bytes as options and width when present, and passes the remaining bytes as Markdown. Its mode bits select document parsing, file parsing, incremental parser feeds, or Markdown-to-HTML conversion.
The harness masks parser options to seven named bits, including CMARK_OPT_VALIDATE_UTF8; the input can leave that bit unset.

For a quoted attribute, the after HTML-tag scanner's high-byte bitmap permits an isolated 0x80 byte to remain in the quoted state, then permits the closing quote and '>' to complete the tag. The scanner-level input beginning `a x="\x80">` is a concrete path.
The before HTML-tag scanner rejects an isolated 0x80 byte in the same quoted-attribute state: its high-byte bitmap does not continue the quote loop, and the fallback goes to the rejecting state.

The harness has several potential routes to the same parser behavior. Document parsing calls S_parser_feed directly; incremental feeding also calls S_parser_feed; Markdown-to-HTML conversion delegates to document parsing. These routes prevent treating the incremental mode alone as the complete coverage assessment.

evidence.dependency_reason: Document parsing forwards Markdown bytes to S_parser_feed.
Incremental feeding forwards each chunk to S_parser_feed.
The conversion route delegates to document parsing.

facts.statement: The supplied recipe runs CMake and builds cmark_static, then compiles the fuzz entry and links it with libcmark.a.
The complete supplied harness contains no assertion that an HTML tag is recognized. For non-null documents it renders five formats, frees their results, and frees the document.
